369 -> 381, and every one of the twelve is a finding the rule could not see rather than a query anyone added: `search_read` and `name_search` joined `_QUERY_METHODS`. All twelve are `for x in <records>:` with a query inside -- three in `approval_dashboard._compute_bottlenecks`, and one each in `account_payment_register`, `pos_config`, `stock_picking`, `project_task`, `product_template`, `website` (x2), `project_timesheet_holidays` and `res_country`. Judged one by one before being added.

WHAT WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED, so it is not re-proposed: treating `while` as a loop adds 13 findings and every one is a worklist or paging loop issuing a BATCHED query per iteration (`Lot.search(name in candidates)`); comprehensions add 4, all short-circuiting `any(...)`; `read` adds 42, dominated by `file.read()` and `self.device.read()`; `_search` adds 15, mostly loops over a handful of domains. `test_while_loop_not_flagged` is right and now has the evidence for it.

First baseline. The floor used to be a Python literal in the test module; twenty-four of test_lint's last forty commits changed nothing there but an integer and the comment above it, and five of the six gates red at 598cf211cc2 were floor drift rather than defects. `assert_ratchet` now takes a gate name and refuses an integer outright, so a floor cannot go back into Python. Measured at CI scope -- `--addons-path=odoo/addons,addons`, only test_lint installed -- against a `git archive` of HEAD carrying this change and nothing else, because the shared checkout holds other sessions' uncommitted work.
